tool_input.command:
git -C <repo> commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(doctor): tie the sandbox platform guard to its build tag

Copilot: procgroup_windows.go's comment claimed hookInvocationObserved
"returns via errSandboxUnsupportedPlatform before ever constructing a
command on any GOOS reaching this file." The guard was
`sandboxGOOS == "windows"` while the file is tagged `!unix`, so the
sentence was false for plan9 and js/wasm — execution would proceed with
process-group cleanup silently a no-op.

Verified before fixing, and it changes the severity: internal/doctor
does not build for plan9 or js/wasm at all today, via
internal/enable → internal/resolve → internal/process, whose tree.go
carries `//go:build linux || darwin || windows`. The claim was
vacuously true in practice and wrong about the mechanism — a comment
that turns into a lie the moment that transitive constraint widens,
with nothing to catch it.

Fixed structurally, not with a better sentence. sandboxSupported is
declared in the same tagged pair that already decides whether the
process-group primitives are real (true in procgroup_unix.go, false in
procgroup_windows.go), and hookInvocationObserved gates on it. Guard and
build tag are now one fact declared once; adding a platform to one side
means editing the other. Same lesson as S1's containment self-test —
assert the property, don't enumerate remembered cases.

This exposed one variable standing in for two facts. sandboxGOOS is kept
but narrowed to the only question it answers — does this platform's
FileMode carry execute bits — which is Windows-specific and read solely
by the exec-bit check. "Can the sandbox run" is sandboxSupported, which
is unix-vs-not. The platform sets genuinely differ: on plan9 the exec
bit is meaningful but the sandbox cannot run, so collapsing them would
make one guard wrong. Both doc comments say so, to stop a later
"simplification" merging them.

Tests keep their seam via simulateWindows(t), which moves BOTH — a test
that moves one models a platform that does not exist. The conflation was
confirmed by observation, not argument: switching the guard turned three
green tests red because they set only sandboxGOOS. They pass through the
helper.

GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go vet ./internal/doctor/ clean.
EOF
)" -- internal/doctor/ DESIGN.md
